macro_context.market_sentiment: Broadly risk-on as of May 6, 2026. Major indices at or near record highs: Nasdaq +1.36% to 25,670, Dow +1.14% to 49,854, S&P 500 +1.10% to 7,338.89. Rally driven by peace optimism on a U.S.-Iran nuclear memorandum of understanding nearing completion, with oil prices declining on the news. (Source: TheStreet, Bloomberg, Schwab)
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% at its April 29, 2026 meeting, in a rare 8-4 split vote. Inflation remains above 2% target due to elevated energy prices and tariff pass-through. Market pricing zero rate moves for 2026; one 25bp cut expected in December 2027. April 29 was likely Chair Powell's final meeting. (Source: CNBC, Federal Reserve, Al Jazeera)
macro_context.geopolitical: U.S.-Iran conflict remains the dominant market flashpoint; UAE intercepted Iranian missiles on May 4 causing a brief selloff, but peace hopes drove a sharp recovery by May 6. Additional risks: U.S. tariff uncertainty, Venezuela tensions, NATO posture on Greenland, mid-term election uncertainty, and ongoing Great-Power competition over critical minerals and semiconductors. Energy prices remain elevated but easing on Iran deal hopes. (Source: IMF, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, Kitces)

web_context.competitor_activity: All major health insurers (UNH, Elevance/ELV, Cigna/CI, Humana/HUM) beat Q1 2026 estimates, with some raising 2026 guidance. Sector-wide headwind is elevated medical costs and Medicare Advantage margin pressure. Humana has fully pivoted to senior/Medicare-only focus, removing itself from commercial competition. CVS/Aetna represents the closest vertically integrated rival. CNBC (May 5, 2026) notes 'major health insurers show signs of recovery but a key test looms' — signaling market concern about whether the Q1 trend can hold through Q2. UNH retains market leadership with ~$450-455B projected 2026 revenue.
